questions: With seven sensors at 0.02 m spacing and a 16 mm footprint, is the signal smoother at the outer sensors, or does it saturate or jump?
Does steering_oscillation rise above the iteration-1 level of about 0.28 on the oval? If so, is the cause the wider array or the larger footprint?
Where does the first off-track event occur (which track, which bend, and at what progress)? Please use per-step telemetry if available.
Does the 16 mm footprint degrade centre tracking (rms_error above about 0.03 m) compared with 12 mm?
Which geometry limit now constrains the controller most: sensor spread, footprint, wheel_track or mass?

intent: Test whether a wider seven-sensor array (±0.06 m, 0.02 m spacing) with a 16 mm footprint keeps a graded line signal at larger lateral error, so that max_error stays under the 0.06 m off-track limit on bends. Drivetrain and body are held at the iteration-1 values to isolate the sensor change. Expected: fewer off-track endings, max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, and progress above 0.5 on the oval.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that the score is driven by progress on the oval, and that off-track endings come from single bend excursions with max_error just above 0.06 m. The next test isolates the sensor array: if max_error falls below 0.06 m with the same drivetrain, the array was the limit. If it does not, the next lever is wheel_track or mass, to tame steering oscillation, and the footprint should be checked separately.
rationale: Iteration 1 raised the score from 52.3 to 114.4, almost entirely through progress on the oval (0.47 mean, up from 0.14). Every run still ends off track, so the limiting problem is edge loss, not general tracking. RMS error is small (0.026 to 0.031 m) while max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.066 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. The robot tracks well until a single excursion carries it past the edge. Steering oscillation rose from about 0.09 to 0.28 on the oval, which fits the narrower, lighter robot responding faster and occasionally overshooting. Body width is not a lever: the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and even at 0.18 m that gives 0.0575 m, so the 0.06 m floor governs. The sensor array is the geometry lever that matters. With five sensors at 0.025 m spacing over ±0.05 m, the outer sensors lose the tape once the robot is roughly 0.03 m off centre, so the signal saturates in exactly the bends where the excursion happens. I therefore make three geometry changes: (1) extend to seven sensors at 0.02 m spacing over ±0.06 m, so a graded reading persists to larger lateral error and the weighted average does not saturate; (2) enlarge the footprint from 12 mm to 16 mm, widening each sensor's capture band so the tape is seen across a wider range of offsets; (3) hold wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg, body_length 0.14 m, body_width 0.10 m and sensor lead 0.03 m, so the drivetrain and dynamics are unchanged and the effect of the sensor change can be read cleanly. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, fewer off-track endings, and progress above 0.5 on the oval. Risk: the 16 mm footprint lowers the spatial resolution near centre and may add jitter, and the seven-sensor sum may amplify noise. I ask the Integrator to report whether the signal is smoother at the edges and whether steering oscillation rises.
